Subject: Q4 token overage and approaching renewal — can we discuss options?

Hi Hannah,

Hope you had a good holiday — quick note as we start planning our budget cycle. We just closed out Q4 and saw a material overage relative to our committed plan (attached CSV). Committed: 120M tokens/month; actual: 185M tokens/month in Dec 2026 (~54% over). That pushed our costs up and triggered internal concerns about predictability for next year.

We value Redwood's latency and the caching gains, but Procurement is flagging the delta and wants options before our Jan renewal date. Two asks: 1) Can you share a short analysis tying the overage to usage patterns (bursting vs. steady uplift)? 2) We'd like a written proposal for a flexible capacity option or short-term uplift with pricing and term tradeoffs.

I attached our raw usage export and a snapshot of the latency dashboard. Could we get a 30-min call this week? Prefer Tue/Wed morning PST.

Thanks —
Samantha

Hi Samantha — thanks for sending the exports. Took a quick pass and summarized below, and happy to jump on a call Tue 1/12 10am PST if that works.

Top-line from our first pass:
- Committed: 120M tokens/mo; Dec actual: 185M tokens (avg daily spike on 12/14–12/21).
- Burst vs steady: ~70% of overage came from bursty search/summary jobs tied to a marketing campaign; remaining ~30% was sustained uplift across chat endpoints.
- Unit economics: effective per-1k-token cost on hosted usage this quarter was $0.0046 after credits and volume tiers; without a capacity change, projected spend for the next 12 months at current burn = ~ $10.2M (vs current committed model ~ $6.0M).

Proposal options (short bullets) — detailed doc attached if helpful:
A) Short-term uplift (2 months) — +40M/mo committed at current committed rate, 60-day review window. Low friction; limited discount.
B) Flexible capacity (recommended) — baseline commit remains 120M, auto-burst allowance to 180–200M with blended pricing: committed rate applies to baseline, burst billed at 60% of list hosted price (smoothing cap). Includes 90-day review and automatic rebase if sustained uplift >3mo.
C) Term change + volume discount — move to 12-month commitment of 200M with a stepped discount (5–12% depending on final term/volume). Best long-run unit-cost but requires longer commit.

Attachments: proposed_flex_pricing_v3.pdf — includes modeled ROI for the three options and DocuSign-ready quote for Option B.

If you want, I can loop in Lauren for contractual tweaks and Connor for ops feasibility on burst windows.

Cheers,
Hannah

Hi all — jumped on Hannah's analysis. Ops notes:
- We can support auto-burst to 200M for OliveCo with minimal engineering changes. The main risk is tail latency during large coordinated campaigns; we recommend setting a soft concurrency cap and using prefix caching for the summary jobs you mentioned.
- Implementation: rule-based auto-burst policy (region: us-west), KV cache warmup window of 5–10 minutes. We can enable this as a config change on your Dedicated pool within 24–48 hours after agreement.
- Monitoring: we'll enable a per-route throttling dashboard and an alert that fires when burst billing > 20% of monthly spend.

Operational impact: moderate; no infra migration required. We'll add a one-time ops fee of $3,500 for policy setup and runbook handoff (it covers our runbook, alerting, and a 2-hour onboarding session).

Connor

Hi Samantha — quick note from a CS/ROI angle. Thanks for the raw export — we ran a short eval on top-10 routes. Findings:
- The marketing campaign compression produced a ~2.4x increase in tokens for a single endpoint (summary endpoint). However, completion quality held steady — higher customer value per token for that campaign window.
- Projected savings under Option B (Flexible capacity) vs no-change model: ~22% annualized cost reduction in year 1 due to lower effective burst unit price and fewer emergency uplift purchases.
- Adoption plan: we'll supply a set of 5 sanity prompts and a traffic shaping guide to limit extreme tails. We'll also provide a monthly digest with token forecasts and suggested rebase actions.

Open items:
- Procurement: confirm whether OliveCo requires PO up front for the ops fee.
- Legal: Lauren, happy to work through any SOW language for the setup fee and burst caps.

Happy to present the ROI slide on the call.
